messages:
customer-alex: Hey team — we've been seeing a spike of 429s and timeouts on Dedicated (tenant: brightlane) when users send long-context prompts (~30k tokens). Started ~14:05 UTC. Symptoms: elevated latency, repeated KV evictions, and downstream auth retries.

support-ian: Thanks Alex — sorry about that. Can you paste a sample request id and approximate timeframe? Also which Dedicated pool/region?

customer-alex: Request IDs: req_2048a7, req_2048b5 around 2026-01-22T14:06:10Z. Region: us-west-2 - dedicated-pool-3. We're on model rwd-llama-13b-quant.

maria.g: Noted. I can see eviction churn in the logs for that pool. Quick snippet from node logs (~14:06):

```
[kvcache] evict key=tenant:brightlane:ctx:abcd size=2.3MB reason=fragmentation
[kvcache] coalesce miss prefix_hits=0 sessions=112 active_longctx=18
[runtime] alloc_fail: slab_realloc failed: OOM? free_pages=120
```

maria.g: There are repeated evict waves every ~3-7s. Looks like long-context sessions cause big KV entries -> fragmentation and small free spans.

jonathan.k: Do we have autoscale events at that time? Could be cooldown prevented additional nodes.

eng-lee: Checking autoscale logs. I see a scale decision at 14:04 to add 1 node but scale-back cooldown prevented additional adds until 14:10 due to previous flapping. So throughput remained on the same set and memory pressure grew.

support-ian: So summary: long-context workload -> large KV objects -> slab fragmentation -> repeated evictions -> auth retries and 429s.

customer-alex: Any quick mitigations we can apply? Our users are getting errors right now.

maria.g: Temporary mitigations: 1) reduce tenant max_context to 16k tokens if possible; 2) disable prefix caching for brightlane (shaves large KV entries); 3) set tenant-specific priority to burst capacity; 4) bump slab_compact interval to run sooner.

eng-lee: I can flip #2 and schedule a one-off slab_compact run. Will take ~30s to propagate. Anyone object?

support-ian: Go ahead. Also capture pprof/kv-stats while you do it. Use: 

```
curl -sS "http://node-host:9611/debug/pprof?seconds=30" -o /tmp/pprof-node.pb
curl -sS "http://node-host:9200/_kv/stats?tenant=brightlane"
```

maria.g: Also please collect the eviction trace: 
```
journalctl -u redwood-kv -o cat --since "2026-01-22T14:00:00" --until "2026-01-22T14:12:00" > /tmp/kv-evict.log
```

eng-lee: Done. I disabled prefix caching for brightlane and triggered slab_compact. Early signs: eviction rate dropped by ~60% after compaction. Pprof shows high free list fragmentation before compaction.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0137 assigned to eng-runtime. Priority: P2. Link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-0137

jonathan.k: Next steps: 1) run a targeted compaction policy for the pool; 2) increase autoscale headroom to allow faster ramp for heavy longctx; 3) add tenant-level guardrails (max_context & kv-entry-size); 4) investigate allocator improvements to reduce fragmentation (slab merging or large object pool).

maria.g: I'll open a follow-up RFC for allocator changes. For now, I've pushed a conservative change to autoscaler to reduce scale cooldown from 6m -> 2m for dedicated-pool-3 (trial window 1h).

customer-alex: Thanks, saw errors subside. Do you want us to limit long-context clients on our end?

support-ian: If you can soft-limit new long requests for the next hour while we monitor, that would help. We'll keep you updated.

eng-lee: Added monitoring alert for KV eviction_rate > 50/s and longctx_active > 10 per node. I'll watch for regressions.

maria.g: Action items: [maria.g] RFC allocator, [eng-lee] autoscale tuning rollback plan, [jonathan.k] coordinate capacity increase for brightlane, [support-ian] communicate mitigation to customer, [customer-alex] apply soft-limits.

customer-alex: Confirmed — will rate-limit on client side for 1h. Thanks everyone. :pray:

support-ian: Closing loop once we verify stable for 2h. If anything spikes, please ping this thread. :thumbsup:
